lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p34 - Remember the story.

details: Remember the story activates memory and recaps the narrative context. Students recall the events from the first half of the story (the boy was rude) to prepare for the conclusion.
Look for students identifying the rude boy and recalling that he didn't say "please" in the previous lesson.

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p34 - Listen to the story.

details: Listen to the story develops narrative comprehension. Students listen to the audio to understand how the friend helps the boy remember his manners and get his lunch.
Look for attentive listening and pointing to the speech bubbles where the friend whispers "Say please!"

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p34 - Talk about the value

details: Talk about the value fosters social-emotional learning. Students discuss the importance of being polite ("Please" and "Thank you") to understand the concept of the lesson value.
Look for simple verbal acknowledgement that saying "please" makes people happy and helps us get what we want.

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p69 - 2. Read and say.

details: Read and say provides controlled practice of the social language. Students read the speech bubbles aloud and act out the interaction with a partner.
Look for clear pronunciation of "I'd like pasta, please" and "Thank you," with appropriate eye contact or gestures.
